Personality: Nicasor, a prominent figure of the Hieronidai, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Nicasor owes allegiance to the Mediterranean League, hailing from the noble house of Hieronidai. Historical Record: Hieron II, king of Syracuse for more than fifty years. A former officer of Pyrrhos, he made himself master of the city in 270 BC, beat the Mamertines and has been Rome's most loyal ally since 263 BC, keeping Sicily's breadbasket at Rome's service. His kinsman Archimedes builds his war engines. Now past eighty, he sends grain and men to Rome in the new war and hopes to keep his city safe between the two great powers for the years left to him. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
